title: Part 1.II — Antinomies of Definition
role: Burke develops a parallel analytical apparatus to the pentad: a substance vocabulary tracking the multiple senses in which philosophical and rhetorical discourse fixes 'what a thing is.' The chapter opens by tracing the Indo-Germanic root *sta- (the etymological background to 'substance,' 'status,' 'stance') and moves through contextual, familial, dialectical, and tragic substance, the Burkean distinction between actus and status (act-as-process vs. condition-of-being), and intrinsic/extrinsic definition. The substance vocabulary cross-cuts the pentad — especially the Act-Agent ratio via actus/status — and supplies the rhetorical mechanics of how motive-statements stabilize ambiguous referents. The chapter is the canonical source for the Phase 3 substance-vocabulary synthesis deliverable. It is also the OCR-flagged chapter of the volume: italic technical terms (Indo-Germanic 'stā', adverbs ending in -tly such as 'explicitly', 'sufficiently') show period-substitution and italic-tl cluster mangling that Phase 2 must normalize before concept extraction.
internal_section_headings_note: All 13 subsection headings confirmed from published TOC (PDF p.6). This is the most subsection-dense Part 1 chapter — Burke moves the substance vocabulary through 13 distinct moves in 38 pages. Phase 2 must preserve these as Tier-1 chunk boundaries.
